title: Capstone: Ship a Small Release
description: Plan and model a focused release using branches, commits, integration, and tags.

blocks.content: A release is due. You need to make a clean branch, commit a focused change, merge it, and leave a traceable tag. What is the smallest Git action that keeps the work safe?

A release workflow combines the habits you practiced: make a branch, stage intentional changes, commit clearly, merge after review, and tag the release.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Working files"] -->|"choose an action"| B["Git history"] -->|"share or recover"| C["Team project"]
```

blocks.question: Which release step makes a named, permanent marker?
blocks.explanation: A tag names a specific commit, which makes a release easy to find later.

blocks.starterCode:
const release = { branch: "release-notes", commits: 1, tag: "v1.0.0" };
console.log(release);

blocks.prompt: Build `releasePlan(branch, commits, tag)`. Export it and return an object with those three values plus `ready`, which is true only when the branch has at least one commit and the tag starts with `v`.

tests.description: marks a tagged branch with a commit as ready
does not release an empty branch
